subject: API latency drift — advisory and follow-up (Glint Labs)
messages:
From: Redwood On-Call <oncall@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Morales <sara@glintlabs.com>, ops+glint@glintlabs.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, ava.chen@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Notice: elevated P95 latency for hosted inference in us-west (Glint tenant)

Hi Sara / Glint ops team,

We wanted to let you know we observed a sustained increase in P95 request latency for your hosted API routes starting ~07:30 PST (us-west). The impact:
- 07:30–08:00: P95 rose from ~140ms to ~420ms for standard text-generation routes
- Error rates remained low (<0.5% 5xx), but tail latency affected streaming responsiveness

Immediate actions we’re taking:
- Routing new requests to alternate healthy pools within us-west to reduce exposure
- Rolling a targeted runtime patch to an instance group that shows memory pressure patterns
- Increasing autoscaler thresholds to let additional capacity come online faster

We do not expect data loss. We’ve opened incident RED-20261130-GLNT and published a live advisory: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-11-30-latency-drift.

If this is causing visible production impact for Glint (errors or user-facing failures), please reply here and we’ll prioritize an accelerated remediation and a credit review. We’ll send an hourly update until the trend is resolved.

— Redwood On-Call
(attachment: incident-log-20261130.csv)
From: Sara Morales <sara@glintlabs.com>
To: Redwood On-Call <oncall@redwood.ai>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ops+glint@glintlabs.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:27:46 -0800
Subject: Re: Notice: elevated P95 latency for hosted inference in us-west (Glint tenant)

Thanks for the heads up — we saw degraded response times in our dashboard and had a spike in support tickets. Two quick asks:
1) Can you confirm whether these requests hit our pinned model version or a fallback replica?
2) We rely on streaming for our UI; any mitigation timeline?

We appreciate the update and the status link; please loop in our CSM if credits are being considered.

— Sara
Head of Platform, Glint Labs
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Morales <sara@glintlabs.com>, ops+glint@glintlabs.com
Cc: ava.chen@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:05:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Notice: elevated P95 latency for hosted inference in us-west (Glint tenant)

Sara — thanks for the quick reply and sorry for the disruption. Quick answers and next steps: 
- Routing/model: traffic for your routes is currently split 85/15 between your pinned model version and a compatible fallback variant; we’re forcing 100% to the pinned model in the next 10–15m while we verify kernel patch behavior.
- Timeline: we’ve already routed to alternate healthy pools; we expect visible improvement within 20–45 minutes. If not, we’ll fail over to a dedicated pool in another region and keep latencies below the SLO while we finish the rollback.

I’m keeping this thread as the single coordination channel. Ava (runtime lead) is on the patch and will post hourly updates. Marissa from CSM will coordinate any billing/credit reconciliation after we stabilize.

Action items I’ll own:
- Confirm exact replica mix + send a short CSV of sampled request traces (attached).
- Open a credit review ticket if end-user impact > 5 minutes of elevated P95 across your production routes.

I’ll update shortly — thanks for your patience.

— Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachment: p95-trend-graph.png)
From: ava.chen@redwood.ai <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Morales <sara@glintlabs.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Post-incident follow-up: root cause, mitigation, and next actions (Glint Labs)

Hi Sara / Glint ops team,

Posting the post-incident summary and immediate next steps after the remediation on 2026-11-30: 
Summary of root cause (short):
- A mis-tuned autoscaler threshold on a subset of our us-west instance groups delayed capacity addition under a transient workload spike. Concurrently, a recent runtime scheduler patch caused slightly higher memory residency on older replica pools; together these factors drove P95 tail increases.

Mitigations applied:
- Rolled back the scheduler patch for affected pools and promoted healthy pools into the routing ring (complete: 2026-11-30T09:38 PST)
- Tightened autoscaler instance group thresholds and added a short-circuit bypass for high-priority tenant routes
- Added sampling to your tenant’s route for earlier drift detection and a dedicated alert escalation in our pager path

Customer impact and compensation:
- We observed ~32 minutes of elevated P95 for Glint’s production routes between 07:30–08:02 PST with no elevated error rate. Marissa will follow up on a one-time service credit to cover user support hours.

Planned actions (next 30 days):
- Engineering: Add per-tenant autoscaler guards and increase eviction telemetry retention (ETA: 2 weeks)
- Product: Expose a per-route pinning policy in Console for guaranteed single-variant routing (ETA: 4 weeks)
- Ops: Run a simulated spike test for us-west with the updated autoscaler rules (ETA: 1 week)

Attachments: incident-log-20261130.csv (sampled traces)

Please reply with any follow-up questions or if you’d like a short sync to review the postmortem; we can schedule a 30-min run-through this week.

Thanks again for your patience — we’re committed to preventing recurrence.

— Ava Chen
Runtime Lead, Redwood Inference
